Hi Marissa,

Thanks — recap looks right. A few clarifications from procurement's perspective:
- Confirmed current: ~200M tokens/month.
- Ramp plan: we expect to hit ~600M by month 6 and ~1.2B by month 12 if adoption continues.
- Marketplace priority: AWS first, GCP second. We may pilot Azure later, but don't need Azure pricing for procurement sign-off initially.

Target budget: our finance team is aiming for a gross marketplace spend in the range of $50k–$90k per month at scale; rough back-of-envelope target is roughly $50–$80 per 1M tokens (gross on the marketplace), but we are flexible if you can show better unit economics once marketplace fees are accounted for.

Please include any tiered-volume discounts and note the assumed marketplace fee percentages for AWS/GCP.

I'll loop in procurement if you need formal pricing docs.

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer unit price mapping — proposed mapping and math

Samir —

Appreciate the clarity on targets. Below is a concise proposed mapping plus the math so procurement has a clean reference. All numbers are per 1M input+output tokens.

Assumptions:
- Redwood target net (what we keep after marketplace fees) = $60 / 1M tokens
- Marketplace fees: AWS = 20% (typical private offer fee structure), GCP = 15%, Azure = 10% (we can adjust if marketplace contact disagrees)

Gross list price needed on marketplace to deliver $60 net: 
- AWS gross = 60 / (1 - 0.20) = $75.00 / 1M tokens
- GCP gross = 60 / (1 - 0.15) ≈ $70.59 / 1M tokens
- Azure gross = 60 / (1 - 0.10) = $66.67 / 1M tokens

Tiered volume discounts (applied to gross marketplace price):
- 0–499M tokens/mo: list price = as above
- 500M–999M tokens/mo: 10% off gross price
- 1B+ tokens/mo: 20% off gross price

Example: For AWS at 1B/mo (20% discount): gross before discount $75 → after 20% discount $60. Redwood net = $60 * (1 - 0.20) = $48 (this would be below our target net $60, so we recommend Redwood keep the net target and apply discounting primarily via longer-term committed spend or blended unit price). We can structure the private offer so the contracted net to Redwood meets your target while offering procurement a clean, single gross number on the AWS invoice. 

Alternative pricing constructs we can support:
- Blended unit price in the private offer that guarantees Redwood gets $60 net across committed volume tiers.
- Upfront commitment credits (prepaid) that reduce effective $/1M.

Attachments included:
- Redwood_AWS_Private_Offer_Template.pdf (sample private offer term sheet)
- Marketplace_Unit_Price_Mapping.csv (CSV with the mapping table and formulae)

Requests:
1) Confirm whether the $50–$80 / 1M tokens gross target you mentioned is the range procurement prefers; if so, we’ll tune the net/gross split to hit the higher end via commitment discounts.
2) If Julia/AWS Marketplace has different fee assumptions, flag them and we’ll recalc immediately.

If that looks reasonable I can draft a sample private offer with the gross listing prices for AWS and GCP and route it to procurement/Julia for review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Marissa —

Next steps from our side: procurement will review the templates and Julia will confirm AWS fee assumptions. If everything aligns we’ll ask for a formal private offer (DocuSign) we can sign and move to a pilot.

Please draft the sample private offer for AWS (and a GCP analog) and share the DocuSign link when ready.

—Samir
